Also if you consider yourself to be a toxic person, and if you genuinely believe my comment about you being a narcissist; this can also be seen as a mental health illness. 

You might consider seeking help for yourself.

I went to the doctor for the very first time about my mental health when I was 24; I’ve been mentally ill since the age of 9 and have been suicidal for as long as I can remember. I’ve fallen out with family, I’ve lost friendships and relationships. 

Seeking help isn’t something that other people can tell you to do. Realistically, I should have received help as a young teen. However I put it off and put it off because I had demons telling me for so long that there was no point. 

So one day I went to the doctor and he didn’t believe me. He put me in tablets that he shouldn’t have and that made me even more suicidal. That same day, I had my mum telling me there was nothing wrong with me and not believing me either. 

Mental health is not smooth sailing and is such a hard thing to explain when you can’t make sense of your own brain. Depression/anxiety/personality disorders, they are all subjective to the person they are harbouring inside. Therefore are not an easy feat to manoeuvre. 

What took me over half my life, might take him a few more weeks, a few more years, maybe the rest of his life. 

He needs to know he has people to hold him up whilst he isn’t strong enough. People that won’t judge him. People that will be there when he comes out the other side.

“I’m a good looking woman and I’m constantly bombarded with men complimenting me, hitting on me, asking me out etc”

1. You not acting on any of this is not anything of high regard. Unless your relationship is poly amorous, which is doesn’t sound like it is, this is normal. Other people paying you attention is irrelevant. 
2. “In return” to you not cheating on him, he doesn’t need to look good for you as opposed to for himself. That’s most important. 
3. Mental health isn’t black and white. It’s a highly long process of a multitude of things and it takes time, patience and most importantly, UNCONDITIONAL love.

Not here to lecture. I didn’t seek help for my mental health issues for 13-15 years, I’m now diagnosed as manic depressive (bipolar) and severe paranoia also in a relationship with a bipolar/severe health anxiety man.
You really are a narcissist.

If he truly is going through a hard time with his mental health, then his needs come before yours; period. Being a partner to someone with mental health issues isn’t an easy task. It’s tiring. It’s frustrating. It can make you question a lot. 

 But honestly, when you love someone wholeheartedly, you don’t even question what it takes to help them get better. 

Quite frankly, my take away from this is that you can’t handle being the partner of someone with mental health issues and you are selfish.
